records.original_target_statement:
Let $`K`$ be the convolution kernel on $`\mathbb R`$ whose Fourier transform is $`\widehat K(\xi)=\tanh\xi/\xi`$, extended continuously at zero. Does there exist $`c>1`$ and an even continuous profile $`v:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)`$, smooth away from zero, strictly decreasing for $`x>0`$, and tending to zero at infinity, such that

```math
K*v=c^2v-\frac{3c}{2}v^2+\frac12v^3,\qquad v(0)=c\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt3}\right)?
```

The associated surface profile is $`\eta=cv-v^2/2`$, with $`\eta(0)=c^2/3`$. These profiles yield a traveling solution $`(\eta(x-ct),v(x-ct))`$ of

```math
\partial_t\eta+\partial_x(K*v+\eta v)=0,\qquad\partial_tv+\partial_x(\eta+v^2/2)=0.
```

# Comparison with AIM 162

Target: [An extreme solitary wave for the bidirectional Whitham system](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/162-extreme-bidirectional-solitary-wave.md),
revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`.
Paper: [An extreme solitary wave for the bidirectional Whitham system](paper/manuscript.pdf),
Kaiwen Jin, 15 October 2026.

This comparison uses the finished manuscript and the public problem statement.
It presents a complete affirmative solution claim for mathematical review.

| Original requirement | Result and location in the paper | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Real-line convolution kernel with Fourier symbol `tanh(xi)/xi`, continuously extended by 1 at zero | Equations (2) and (6); Fourier convention at the end of Section 1 | Exact symbol and mass-one normalization |
| Existence of a speed `c>1` | Theorem 1.1 and Lemma 4.3 | One speed, also satisfying `c<sqrt(3(sqrt(3)-1))` |
| An even continuous profile from the real line to the positive reals | Theorem 1.1; Lemmas 4.1 and 4.4 | Entire real line; strict positivity |
| Smoothness away from zero and strict decrease for positive x | Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 1.1 | Smooth on the punctured line; strict decrease on the whole positive half-line |
| Tending to zero at infinity | Lemma 4.3, using the balance in Lemma 4.2 | Both tails vanish; profile integrability is not assumed |
| Cubic equation `K*v=c^2 v-(3c/2)v^2+v^3/2` and crest `v(0)=c(1-1/sqrt(3))` | Equation (3), Proposition 3.3, Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 1.1 | Pointwise equation on the whole line, including the crest |
| Surface profile `eta=cv-v^2/2` with `eta(0)=c^2/3` | Theorem 1.1 and its closing proof | Exact profile reconstruction and crest identity |
| Both printed conservative PDEs for the traveling pair | Equations (1) and (23), and the proof of Theorem 1.1 | Globally in distributions; classically away from the moving crest |
| Estimates adequate for the growing-period construction | Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 2.5; Propositions 3.2--3.3 and Lemma 4.1 | Common modulus and drop; fixed-period smoothing constants may depend on the period |

The argument for highest positive waves at every sufficiently large period
is supplied in Section 3. Its global continuation uses Constantin--Strauss--
Varvaruca, Theorem 4, Remarks 3--4 and Figure 2 in preprint NI14051, pp.14--15;
the paper checks the full trivial line, transversality, Fredholm condition and
compact exhaustion there. The unique distinguished continuation is the source
input for the same-arm return argument, which is proved in Proposition 3.2.

The fixed-period multiplier, nodal and local smoothing inputs come from
Ehrnström--Johnson--Claassen, Proposition 2.7, Theorem 4.2 and Lemma 4.1,
with numbering tied to arXiv:1610.02603v2. Their Appendix B is credited for
positive highest waves at its fixed period. The real analytic implicit-function
input is Fučík--Nečas--Souček--Souček, Lemma 3R, printed p.57. The normalized
kernel and the stated extreme-solitary question are in Ehrnström--Mæhlen--
Varholm, Section 4.2 and Remark 4.8. All entries and public links appear in the
manuscript bibliography.

Nilsson--Wang's small solitary waves and Ehrnström--Nik--Walker's construction
for the unidirectional square-root multiplier are background comparisons. The
manuscript supplies the large-period positive construction and the zero-tail
argument for the bidirectional cubic itself. It makes no uniqueness, stability,
all-speed, integrable-tail or full Euler-wave claim.

records.original_target_statement:
Fix $`d\ge1`$, $`T>0`$, and a smooth nonnegative compactly supported probability density $`m_{\rm in}`$ on $`Q=\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d`$. For each $`0\le\nu\le1`$, let $`m_\nu`$ be the density component minimizing

```math
\mathcal J(m,a)=\int_0^T\!\int_Q\left(\frac{|a|^2}{2m}+\frac{m^2}{2}\right)dx\,dv\,dt+\frac12\int_Q m(T)^2dx\,dv
```

subject to

```math
\partial_tm+v\cdot\nabla_xm-\nu\Delta_vm+\nabla_v\cdot a=0,\qquad m(0)=m_{\rm in}.
```

Admissible pairs have narrowly continuous probability densities with finite second velocity moment, the equation holds distributionally, and $`\mathcal J<\infty`$; use $`|a|^2/m=0`$ at $`(m,a)=(0,0)`$ and $`+\infty`$ when $`m=0`$, $`a\ne0`$. Does there exist an exponent $`\eta=\eta(d)>0`$ such that for every such datum and horizon some $`C<\infty`$, independent of $`\nu`$, satisfies

```math
\|m_\nu-m_0\|_{L^2((0,T)\times Q)}\le C\nu^\eta\qquad(0<\nu\le1)?
```

# Correspondence with AIM problem 405

Target: [An algebraic vanishing-noise rate for kinetic mean-field games](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/405-kinetic-mfg-vanishing-viscosity-rate.md),
repository revision a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22.

The manuscript presents a complete solution claim for this fixed variational
target. Its Theorem 1 gives the requested exponent $`\eta(d)=1/2`$ for every
dimension, and additionally bounds the terminal density difference.
The claim awaits independent mathematical review.

| Original requirement | Manuscript location | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $`Q=\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d`$, without a bounded velocity truncation | Section 1 defines $`Q,S,D`$; Sections 2–4 work on the full velocity space | Same domain; the unit-period torus convention is explicit |
| Every integer $`d\geq1`$ and every $`T>0`$ | Theorem 1 | All prescribed dimensions and horizons |
| Smooth, nonnegative, compactly supported probability datum | Section 1 and Theorem 1 | Same data class; no strict positivity imposed |
| Every $`0<\nu\leq1`$, compared with the zero-diffusivity minimizer | Theorem 1, equation (4), and the closing proof | Every prescribed diffusivity, not only a selected sequence |
| Quadratic acceleration perspective, local density-square cost, and terminal density-square cost | Equation (1) | Exactly the prescribed three costs |
| Velocity diffusion and acceleration flux in the kinetic equation | Equations (2)–(3) | Exactly the prescribed sign, diffusion block, transport, and initial datum |
| Narrowly continuous probability curves with finite second velocity moments | Section 1; Lemma 1; equations (11) and (15) | Original weak class; uniform moments are derived |
| Distributional equation with actual initial and terminal traces | Equation (3); Sections 3–4; equation (21) | Smoothed initial data converge back to the original datum before minimality is used |
| Finite action and the zero/infinite perspective convention at vacuum | Section 1; equations (23)–(24) | The limiting flux is zero at vacuum and has finite original action |
| Constant independent of $`\nu`$ | Equation (5) and the closing proof | Explicit $`L`$ depends only on $`d,T,\lVert m_{\mathrm{in}}\rVert_2`$, initial moment and entropy |
| Spacetime $`L^2`$ density estimate with some positive exponent | Theorem 1, equation (4) | $`\lVert m_\nu-m_0\rVert_{L^2(S)}\leq2\sqrt L\,\nu^{1/2}`$ |

Here $`m_{\mathrm{in}}`$ denotes the original initial density and $`S=(0,T)\times Q`$.
The row containing $`\lVert m_{\mathrm{in}}\rVert_2`$ uses the $`L^2(Q)`$ norm.

The main value comparison is proved in Sections 2–4. Kinetic Gaussian
averaging gives $`E_\nu\leq E_0`$. For fixed $`\nu`$, the entropy calculation
and removal of the positive convolution produce an inviscid pair with
the same density $`m_\nu`$ and cost at most $`E_\nu+L\nu`$.
The exact midpoint square identity yields equation (4).
The weak entropy argument explicitly treats the noncompact velocity tails.

The research references supply the kinetic question, first-order variational
lineage, and credit for the earlier elliptic entropy/current-velocity identity.
They are not used to impose extra regularity on the minimizing pairs.
The cited functional-analysis inputs from Brezis are the one-dimensional
Sobolev chain rule, reflexive weak compactness, continuous-function density,
and Hilbert representation; the kinetic and weighted-action arguments are
given in the manuscript.

The conclusion is for the minimizing pairs stipulated by the target.
It does not claim a new existence theorem, optimality of the exponent, or
rates for general Hamiltonians or different couplings.

records.original_target_statement:
Fix $`n\ge2`$, $`\beta>0`$, $`\gamma\ge0`$ and $`R>1`$, and put

```math
\Theta(s)=\beta\left(s^5/5+\gamma s^4+2\gamma^2s^3+2\gamma^3s^2\right).
```

For a bounded Lipschitz open set $`\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n`$ and a measurable $`K\subset\Omega`$, define

```math
E_\Theta(K,\Omega)=\min_{\substack{v\in H^1(\Omega),\ 0\le v\le1\\v=1\ {\rm a.e.\ on}\ K}}\left(\int_\Omega|\nabla v|^2dx+\int_{\partial\Omega}\Theta(v)d\mathcal H^{n-1}\right).
```

Writing $`\omega_n=|B_1|`$, is the inequality

```math
E_\Theta(K,\Omega)\ge\min_{1\le r\le R}E_\Theta(B_1,B_r)
```

valid whenever $`|K|=\omega_n`$ and $`|\Omega|\le\omega_nR^n`$? For $`r=1`$ the right side uses $`K=\Omega=B_1`$, so unused insulation is allowed.

# Comparison with AIM problem 400

Target: [Concentric-ball optimality for thermal insulation with radiative heat transfer](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/400-radiative-insulation-concentric-balls.md), revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`.

The submitted manuscript presents an affirmative analytic proof of the complete displayed inequality. The claim is submitted for independent mathematical review.

| Original requirement | Manuscript location and coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Every integer n >= 2, beta > 0, gamma >= 0 and R > 1 | Theorem 1.1 and the parameter declaration before (1.1); no further parameter restriction. |
| The exact radiative polynomial | Equation (1.1), with all four terms and both parameters. Lemma 2.2 treats gamma = 0 and gamma > 0. |
| Every bounded Lipschitz open outer set | Energy (1.2) and Theorem 1.1. Connectedness is not required; the boundary-trace discussion in Section 2 addresses local charts. |
| A merely measurable heated set K contained in the outer set | Energy (1.2), Theorem 1.1 and its interpretation. No boundary regularity of K is imposed. |
| H1 temperatures, 0 <= v <= 1 and v = 1 almost everywhere on K | Energy (1.2). Section 2 justifies attainment of this minimum. |
| Interior boundary trace and Hausdorff boundary integral | Energy (1.2), the trace convention immediately following it, and Section 2. |
| Heated volume equal to the unit-ball volume | Theorem 1.1. This gives the unit-temperature core in Proposition 3.1. |
| Total volume at most the radius-R ball volume | Theorem 1.1. Proposition 3.1 gives radial support within radius R. |
| Minimum over every radius from 1 to R | Equation (1.3). Lemma 2.1 proves the exact ball formula, continuity at radius 1 and existence of the minimum. |
| Bare heated ball and unused insulation | Theorem 1.1 and its following paragraph; Proposition 4.2 permits tail truncation and outer radius 1. |
| Full comparison for every admissible pair | Propositions 3.1, 4.1 and 4.2, assembled in the final proof of Theorem 1.1. |

The proof is analytic. It does not use numerical evidence or a computer-generated certificate. The related quadratic, penalized-volume and inactive-constraint results of Bucur, Nahon, Nitsch and Trombetti are credited in the Introduction; the manuscript proves the remaining radiative constrained comparison by an additional argument. No claim is made for an arbitrary increasing boundary potential or about uniqueness of optimal shapes.

OpenAI Codex assisted with the argument, algebra, source checking and writing. One AI reader and one AI referee reviewed an anonymized earlier draft in fresh contexts on a shared host. These were internal reviews; no separate detailed review report is submitted. Independent mathematical review is requested. A successful build or internal AI review is not community acceptance or formal verification.

records.original_target_statement:
Let $`\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n`$ be a bounded connected smooth domain with $`|\Omega|=1`$, and let $`d_1,d_2,d_3>0`$. Consider the unique global bounded classical solution of

```math
a_t-d_1\Delta a=b(c-a),\qquad b_t-d_2\Delta b=b(c-a),\qquad c_t-d_3\Delta c=-b(c-a),
```

with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Assume $`a_0,b_0,c_0\in C^2(\overline\Omega)`$ are strictly positive and satisfy the Neumann compatibility conditions. Put

```math
M_1=\int_\Omega(a_0+c_0),\qquad M_2=\int_\Omega(b_0+c_0),
```

and assume $`M_2\le M_1<2M_2`$. Is it true that

```math
\lim_{t\to\infty}\left[\|a(t)-M_1/2\|_\infty+\|b(t)-(M_2-M_1/2)\|_\infty+\|c(t)-M_1/2\|_\infty\right]=0?
```

# Comparison with AIM problem 396

Target: [Polynomial decay for KdV with three critical linear modes](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/396-critical-kdv-odd-mode-polynomial-decay.md), revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`.

The submitted manuscript, *Polynomial decay for the Korteweg–de Vries equation at length 14π*, claims the full target with exponent 1/2.

| Original requirement | Manuscript location and result | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Exact real equation y_t+y_x+y_xxx+y y_x=0 on (0,L), L=14π | Equation (1.1), Theorem 1.1 | Identical equation, normalization, scalar field and interval |
| y(t,0)=y(t,L)=y_x(t,L)=0 | Equation (1.1), generator domain (2.1), energy identities (2.4) and (4.1) | Identical boundary realization, with hidden traces for energy solutions |
| Usual energy class C([0,∞);L²)∩L²_loc([0,∞);H¹₀) | Definition preceding Theorem 1.1; Sections 2.1 and 4 | Same class; the mild realization and its public well-posedness sources are stated explicitly |
| Every real datum in one sufficiently small L² ball | Theorem 1.1; Proposition 4.1 | No sign, phase, initial-subspace or additional Sobolev restriction |
| Common δ,C,α>0 before the datum and time quantifiers | Proposition 4.1 chooses fixed times, constants and one δ; closing proof of Theorem 1.1 chooses C | Uniform in every permitted datum; α=1/2 |
| Every t≥0, including zero and intermediate times | Closing proof of Theorem 1.1 | Reciprocal-energy iteration, monotonicity and the initial bounded interval give the bound for all times |
| Three undamped modes and all their mixtures | Lemma 2.1, Proposition 3.2, the exhaustive split in Proposition 4.1 | Stationary mode, conjugate oscillatory pair, every phase and every stable/center mixture |

The complete original decay question follows by choosing the positive exponent α=1/2. The manuscript makes no claim for all critical lengths, large data or optimality of this exponent.

## Public mathematical dependencies

Rosier, Proposition 3.1, supplies the real linear contraction realization. Coron–Crépeau, Proposition 7 and Appendix A, supplies the linear mild maps and usual solution realization. Niu–Xiang, arXiv:2501.13640v2, Lemma 3.2, supplies small-data global existence and uniqueness. Standard one-dimensional Sobolev facts are cited to Brezis. The stable-complement estimate, exact mode classification, quadratic coefficients, whole-center lower bound, rough-data remainder, energy loss and all-time iteration are proved in the manuscript.

Nguyen's fixed-window decay argument is the methodological source. Its mixed-frequency limitation is addressed here by retaining the center forcing through Duhamel's formula and choosing only the stable response periodically. Niu–Xiang's near-critical-length theorem is cited for context, with its exclusion of the exact critical length preserved.

records.original_target_statement:
Let $`f\in C^4(U;\mathbb R^N)`$ be strictly hyperbolic near $`0\in U`$, with every characteristic field genuinely nonlinear, and a uniformly strictly convex entropy pair $`(\eta,q)`$ satisfying $`Dq=D\eta Df`$. Write $`S_tu_0`$ for its standard small-total-variation entropy solution of $`u_t+f(u)_x=0`$ on $`\mathbb R`$. Fix $`T,R,M>0`$ and sufficiently small $`\delta>0`$.
For $`0<\varepsilon<e^{-1}`$ consider every approximate flow $`u:[0,T]\to L^1(\mathbb R;U)`$ supported in $`[-R,R]`$ with $`\sup_t\mathop{\mathrm{TV}}\nolimits u(t)\le\delta`$, $`\|u(0)-u_0\|_1\le\varepsilon`$ and $`\|u(t)-u(s)\|_1\le M|t-s|+\varepsilon`$. For a scalar test function $`\phi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^2)`$ define

```math
\mathcal R_{g,h}(s,t;\phi)=\int g(u(s,x))\phi(s,x)\,dx-\int g(u(t,x))\phi(t,x)\,dx+\int_s^t\!\int[g(u)\phi_t+h(u)\phi_x]\,dx\,dr.
```

Assume, for all $`0\le s<t\le T`$,

```math
|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{id},f}|\le\varepsilon(t-s+\varepsilon)\|\phi\|_{W^{1,\infty}},\qquad\mathcal R_{\eta,q}\ge-\varepsilon(t-s+\varepsilon)\|\phi\|_{W^{1,\infty}}\quad(\phi\ge0).
```

Is there $`C=C(f,\eta,U,\delta,T,R,M)`$ such that every such approximation satisfies

```math
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|u(t)-S_tu_0\|_1\le C\sqrt\varepsilon\,|\log\varepsilon|?
```

| Fixed T,R,M>0 and sufficiently small fixed delta | Theorem 1.1, p. 2, and the start of Section 3, p. 4: T=R=M=1; kappa chosen once below delta and the semigroup-domain threshold | Works for every sufficiently small fixed delta; no parameter varies with n |
| Flows into spatial L1 with values in U and support in [-R,R] | Equations (14)–(18), pp. 4–5: disjoint cells in [0,kappa], bounded amplitudes, summable masses and a uniform time modulus | Every approximation has the required range, support and continuity |

| Initial discrepancy at most epsilon from the prescribed datum | Equations (15)–(16), p. 4, and the initial-trace argument, pp. 4–5: u^(n)(0)=u0 | The same datum is fixed for every n; discrepancy is zero |
| Time modulus M|t-s|+epsilon | Lemma 2.1, equation (9), and equation (18), pp. 3–5: the global modulus is at most (kappa^2/63)|t-s| | Stronger than the required bound with M=1 |
| Conservation residual for every signed scalar Cc1 test and every strip | Equations (1)–(2), Lemma 2.1 and the residual limit (19), pp. 1–5: the vector residual is exactly zero | Includes strips beginning at zero |
| Entropy residual for every nonnegative scalar Cc1 test and every strip | Equations (10)–(12), p. 3, and the bound following (20), p. 5: residual at least -epsilon_n(t-s)||phi_x||infinity | Stronger than the stated epsilon_n(t-s+epsilon_n) test-norm bound |
| Validity of countable sums and residuals at the accumulation point | Equations (17) and (19), p. 5: uniform L1 tails and an explicit bound for both endpoint and spacetime residual differences | No omitted limiting defect or initial-time strip |
| Comparison with the standard small-BV entropy semigroup | Equation (20), p. 5, using Bressan–Guerra Theorem 1.1 | The exact entropy profile is identified with S_t u0 |
| 0<epsilon<e^-1 and a constant depending only on the stated fixed data | Equations (5)–(6), p. 2, and (21), p. 6: epsilon_n=(kappa^4/12)2^(-14n), error=(kappa^2 t/4)2^(-6n), normalized ratio diverges | No finite permitted constant exists; even the initial datum remains fixed |

The only imported PDE theorem used to identify the comparison solution is [Bressan–Guerra, arXiv:2305.10737v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10737v1), Theorem 1.1 on PDF p. 3, with the small-BV domain inclusion described on PDF p. 1. The manuscript verifies strict hyperbolicity, field conditions, strict entropy convexity, exact conservation and entropy inequalities, L1 continuity and domain membership before invoking it. The cited survey supplies background and the rate question; the exact target is the fixed public statement above.

This is an analytic construction. It makes no claim of an optimal modulus, a counterexample for every flux separately, or failure of qualitative convergence. Independent review of the complete argument is requested.

records.original_target_statement:
Let $`0<\lambda<1`$, let $`\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2`$ be bounded and convex, and let $`u`$ be a convex Alexandrov solution with

```math
\lambda\le\det D^2u\le\lambda^{-1}\quad\text{in }\Omega.
```

Here the inequalities mean $`\lambda|E|\le|\partial u(E)|\le\lambda^{-1}|E|`$ for every Borel $`E\subset\Omega`$. Is the distributional Hessian represented by a matrix field satisfying, for every $`\Omega'\Subset\Omega`$,

```math
\sup_{s>0}s^{p_\lambda}\bigl|\{x\in\Omega':|D^2u(x)|>s\}\bigr|<\infty,\qquad p_\lambda=\frac{1+\lambda^2}{1-\lambda^2}?
```

This is the conjectured endpoint weak-$`L^{p_\lambda}`$ estimate, not merely integrability with some unspecified exponent larger than one.

# Comparison with AIM Problem 390

Target: [Sharp weak integrability of planar Monge–Ampère Hessians](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/390-planar-monge-ampere-sharp-hessian-integrability.md), revision a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22.

The manuscript's Theorem 1.1 uses the same Alexandrov measure inequalities and proves local strong integrability at the target power. This implies the requested weak estimate for every positive threshold.

| Original requirement | Manuscript location | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| Every $`0<\lambda<1`$ | Theorem 1.1; Proposition 3.1; final proof | Same full range; a finite integer $`m>K+1`$ is available for each $`K=\lambda^{-1}>1`$ |
| Bounded convex planar domain | Theorem 1.1; Section 2 | Same PDE domain class; no boundary value or periodicity imposed |
| Convex Alexandrov solution with the bounds on every Borel set | Equation (1.1); Proposition 2.1 | Identical measure hypotheses; the density and coordinate identities are obtained in this class |
| Full distributional Hessian represented by a matrix field | Section 2, localized higher integrability; Proposition 2.1 | The whole weak Hessian is a field; no singular part is discarded |
| Every $`\Omega'\Subset\Omega`$ | Theorem 1.1; final proof | Finite cover of the compact image $`Y(\overline{\Omega'})`$ |
| Exact $`p_\lambda=(1+\lambda^2)/(1-\lambda^2)`$ | Theorem 1.1; Proposition 3.1; final proof | $`p_\lambda=1+2/(K^2-1)`$, exactly |
| Finite supremum over all positive thresholds | Equation (1.3); final proof | Follows from the strong integral by the pointwise power bound |
| Public imported results | Section 2; Lemma 3.1; bibliography | Baseline Sobolev regularity, planar strict convexity, Lipschitz area formula and normalized quasiconformal estimates are identified where used; the local projection and area transformation arguments are included |
| Allowed local constant dependence | Introduction; fixed disks in Section 3; final proof | Constants may depend on $`\lambda,u,\Omega'`$; rotation and scale uniformity are established only where used |

The supplementary local argument uses a weighted scalar Lipschitz projection and its residual-set energy estimate. It credits Agazzi et al.'s calibration/projection ideas and does not apply their periodic theorem to a local domain. The exact original-class area transformation is proved in Section 2.

The submitted material is a proposed complete analytic solution claim for mathematical review. Its existence and compilation do not establish AIM acceptance or independent human certification.

records.original_target_statement:
Let $`d\ge1`$ and $`m\ge d+2`$. Fix a smooth compact connected embedded $`d`$-dimensional submanifold $`\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^m`$ without boundary, and assume that it bounds at least one smooth compact connected embedded $`(d+1)`$-dimensional submanifold. Let $`\mathcal F(\Sigma)`$ be the set of all such fillings $`\Omega\subset\mathbb R^m`$ with $`\partial\Omega=\Sigma`$, equipped with their induced Euclidean metrics. Prove or disprove

```math
\sup_{\Omega\in\mathcal F(\Sigma)}\sigma_1(\Omega)=\infty
```

for every such $`\Sigma`$, where $`\sigma_1`$ is the first positive eigenvalue of $`\Delta_\Omega u=0`$, $`\partial_\nu u=\sigma u`$. No bound is imposed on the filling’s volume or topology.

# Correspondence with AIM Problem 112

Target: [Arbitrarily large Steklov frequency with a prescribed embedded boundary](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/112-fixed-embedded-boundary-steklov.md), repository revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`.

Result: [Large Steklov eigenvalues with a prescribed embedded boundary](paper/manuscript.pdf), Theorem 1.1. The note claims the affirmative alternative for the complete problem statement. The following map uses that finished manuscript and the public target.

| Original requirement | Result and location in the paper | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every integer $`d\geq1`$ and $`m\geq d+2`$ | Theorem 1.1; Proposition 2.3 requires filling dimension $`n=d+1\geq2`$ and $`m>n`$; Section 3 treats $`n\geq3`$ and $`n=2`$ | Entire stated dimension/codimension range, including filling codimension one |
| Arbitrary smooth compact connected embedded $`\Sigma^d\subset\mathbb R^m`$, without boundary, admitting at least one smooth compact connected embedded filling | Theorem 1.1; Section 3.1 starts from any such filling. Section 3.2 constructs orientable fillings for every embedded curve and then adds local handles | Every admissible prescribed boundary; no symmetry, unknot or special-position condition |
| The same ambient $`\mathbb R^m`$ and exact boundary $`\partial\Omega=\Sigma`$ | Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 2.3 fix the initial embedding on a neighborhood of the whole boundary; both applications use embeddings into the original ambient space | Pointwise prescribed ambient boundary, not merely an isometric boundary copy |
| Smooth compact connected embedded $`(d+1)`$-dimensional filling | Lemma 2.2 proves smooth embedding and global injectivity; Section 3 takes the image of a compact connected filling | All original regularity, domain topology and embeddedness requirements |
| The final metric is Euclidean induced | Theorem 1.1; Proposition 2.3; Section 3.2 restores original coordinates after the topological graph construction | No replacement of the final ambient metric |
| First positive Steklov eigenvalue with $`\Delta u=0`$, $`\partial_\nu u=\sigma u`$ | Introduction defines $`0=\sigma_0<\sigma_1`$; Section 2 gives the quotient and explicitly translates the source indexing | Same boundary-value problem and first positive eigenvalue |
| For every fixed admissible $`\Sigma`$, the supremum over all such fillings is infinite | For each $`A>0`$, Theorem 1.1 and the end of Section 3 yield $`\sigma_1(\Omega)>A`$; the paragraph after Theorem 1.1 states the equivalent supremum | Complete affirmative conclusion; no bound is claimed uniformly over $`\Sigma`$ |
| No volume or topology bound | Theorem 1.1 and its following paragraph; Section 3.1 keeps one filling, while Section 3.2 permits arbitrarily large genus | No additional bound imposed |

The collar width and approximation parameters may depend on the chosen intrinsic metric and threshold. No limit of the final embedded domains is required. Constants in the surface source estimate are independent of its genus index, as stated where used.

# Scope of the domain clarification

The statement under discussion is
[AIM 423 at revision a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/423-magnetic-airy-half-plane-spectrum.md),
which asks for nonempty spectrum at every real nonzero parameter, including
all intermediate magnitudes.

The note concerns the literal ordinary H1_0 domain in that statement. It
does not resolve the intended spectral question for the different natural
closed magnetic Dirichlet realization.

The [original problem sheet](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/04_AIM_2015/2015-02/2015-02_AIM_Almog_2.pdf)
reports known nonemptiness for sufficiently small and sufficiently large
nonzero magnitudes of the parameter. The remaining intended spectral
question concerns intermediate magnitudes. This note does not extend those
closed-realization spectral results.

| Requirement or interpretation | Result in the note | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Half-plane y>0 and complex L2 | Section 1 fixes exactly this space and geometry | Same |
| Magnetic expression -partial_x^2-(partial_y-i x^2/2)^2+i c y | Equation (1), with no replacement by a nonmagnetic expression | Same |
| Printed ordinary H1_0 and distributional operator expression | Equation (2) defines the restriction T_c | Same literal domain |
| Every real c different from zero, including intermediate magnitudes | Proposition 1 and Section 2 apply for each fixed real c, without a sign or size assumption | All nonzero c covered for the literal restriction; c=0 also satisfies the stated domain result |
| Parameter dependence and convergence | Equation (7) permits a constant C_c depending on the fixed parameter; equations (10)--(11) give strong L2 convergence of functions and operator images | No estimate uniform in c is claimed or needed |
| Closedness of the printed restriction | Section 2 gives an explicit strong graph limit outside its domain | The restriction is nonclosed |
| Spectrum defined by bounded inverse of a bijective shift | Section 3 proves that this inverse property forces closedness | Spectrum of the printed nonclosed restriction is the whole complex plane under this convention |
| Spectrum defined only for closed operators | The printed restriction is nonclosed | The prerequisite is not met |
| Natural closed magnetic Dirichlet realization | Section 3 distinguishes its magnetic Sobolev form domain | Spectral nonemptiness, eigenvalues and a physical threshold are not established here |
| Public imported facts | Brezis, Corollaries 4.23 and 4.24, supply density and uniqueness of locally integrable distributions; Almog--Helffer, pp.6 and12, equations (2.3), (2.4), (2.24), supplies the distinct magnetic-domain prescription | The note states the applications and writes out its graph-limit and bounded-inverse arguments |

The spectrum conclusion does not claim that every spectral point is an
eigenvalue. The distinction between ordinary and covariant derivatives is
part of the result and must be retained in any description of this package.
The note makes no novelty or priority claim.

records.original_target_statement:
Write $`x=(x_1,x_2,z)\in\mathbb R^3`$. Fix $`\varepsilon,c,c_g,\alpha_4>0`$, $`\alpha_5\ge0`$, and an integer $`K\ge2`$. Consider a complex envelope $`u`$ and real electron density $`\rho`$ satisfying

```math
\begin{aligned}i(\partial_t+c_g\partial_z)u+\varepsilon\Delta u+\varepsilon(|u|^2-\rho)u&=-i\varepsilon c\bigl(\alpha_4|u|^{2K-2}u+\alpha_5\rho u\bigr),\\
\partial_t\rho&=\varepsilon\alpha_4|u|^{2K}+\varepsilon\alpha_5\rho|u|^2.\end{aligned}
```

For every Schwartz initial pair $`(u_0,\rho_0)`$ with $`\rho_0\ge0`$, must the local solution extend to all $`t\ge0`$, with $`(u,\rho)\in C([0,\infty);H^m(\mathbb R^3))`$ for every integer $`m\ge3`$? The Laplacian is elliptic in all three spatial coordinates, corresponding to anomalous group-velocity dispersion.

# Comparison with AIM 441

Target: [the immutable problem statement at revision a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/441-ionization-laser-envelope-global-regularity.md).

The question is universal over all its allowed coefficients and Schwartz initial pairs. The note claims its negation through the single admissible witness in Theorem 1.1.

| Original requirement | Result and location in the note | Relation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Space is R^3 with an elliptic Laplacian in all three coordinates | Original system (1.1), Sections 2-4 | Same domain and operator |
| Positive epsilon, c, c_g and alpha_4; alpha_5 nonnegative; integer K at least 2 | Theorem 1.1 selects epsilon=c=c_g=1, alpha_4=delta>0, alpha_5=0, K=2 | One admissible parameter tuple suffices for a counterexample |
| Every Schwartz initial pair with nonnegative density | Section 4.2 constructs nonzero u_0 in C_c^infinity and rho_0=0 | The constructed pair lies in the required class |
| The actual coupled system, including the density equation and optical transport | Sections 3.3 and 4.3 retain the exact moving-frame density translation and reconstruct the physical equations | No uncoupled substitution |
| Local smooth solution with all H^m regularities, m at least 3 | Sections 4.3-4.4 prove physical H^1 uniqueness, recover L^2, and show smooth persistence for every fixed m before T | Same Cauchy solution and solution class |
| Nonnegative electron density | Formula (4.11) gives rho(t,x)=delta integral_0^t abs(u)^4 | Preserved throughout the smooth lifespan |
| Continuation for all nonnegative times | Formula (4.13) proves finite-time divergence of the L^2 gradient norm | Rules out global C_t H^3 continuation and hence the stated universal conclusion |

The imported scalar inverse and linear estimates are identified with their precise versioned sources in Sections 2.1 and 3.1. Their hypotheses are verified in Section 2.4. The new coupling arguments are proved in the note. Appendix A and the exact-arithmetic supplement cover only the stated finite coefficient inequalities. No failure for every parameter, explicit full Cauchy threshold, open-set stability, formal verification or external acceptance is claimed.

records.original_target_statement:
Let $`x\in\mathbb T^3`$, $`q\in B_1(0)\subset\mathbb R^3`$, $`\nu>0`$, $`k>2`$, $`U(q)=-k\log(1-|q|^2)`$ and $`M=Z^{-1}e^{-U}`$. For $`\varepsilon>0`$ consider

```math
u_t+u\cdot\nabla_xu-\nu\Delta_xu+\nabla_xp=\nabla_x\cdot\tau,\quad\nabla_x\cdot u=0,
```



```math
\psi_t+u\cdot\nabla_x\psi=\varepsilon\Delta_x\psi+\nabla_q\cdot\left[\nabla_q\psi+\psi\nabla_qU-(\nabla_xu)q\psi\right],\qquad \tau=\int_{B_1}q\otimes\nabla_qU\,\psi\,dq,
```

with zero configuration-space flux. Fix smooth divergence-free $`u_0`$ and $`\psi_0=M g_0`$, where $`g_0`$ is smooth and bounded above and below by positive constants and $`\int_{B_1}\psi_0(x,q)\,dq=1`$. Can global finite-entropy weak solutions $`(u_\varepsilon,\psi_\varepsilon)`$ be chosen so that, along some $`\varepsilon_j\downarrow0`$, they converge to a global weak solution of exactly the same system with $`\varepsilon=0`$? Require $`u_{\varepsilon_j}\to u`$ strongly in $`L^2`$ on finite time intervals, $`\psi_{\varepsilon_j}\rightharpoonup\psi`$ weakly in $`L^1`$ there, and convergence of the stress and transport fluxes to those computed from $`(u,\psi)`$ in distributions, with no additional defect. Finite entropy means $`\int\psi\log(\psi/M)<\infty`$ and the usual kinetic-fluid entropy inequality.

# Correspondence with AIM problem 376

Original statement: [The zero center-of-mass diffusion limit for kinetic FENE fluids](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/376-fene-vanishing-center-of-mass-diffusion.md), revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`.

Submitted manuscript: *Vanishing center-of-mass diffusion for the three-dimensional FENE dumbbell model*, Kaiwen Jin. Theorem 1.1 is the full-target claim. The locators below refer to the submitted manuscript and its public references.

| Original requirement | Manuscript location and claimed conclusion |
| --- | --- |
| Every nu > 0 and k > 2 on T^3 × B_1(0), with U(q) = −k log(1 − ‖q‖²) and normalized Maxwellian M | Section 1 fixes exactly these parameters, domain, and potential; Theorem 1.1 retains every such parameter. |
| Arbitrary prescribed smooth divergence-free initial velocity | Theorem 1.1 has no size restriction. Section 2.1 handles a nonzero conserved mean by a Galilean translation. |
| Smooth g_0 bounded above and below by positive constants, with configuration mass one | Theorem 1.1 uses this class, including smoothness on the open configuration ball without an extra boundary-derivative hypothesis. Sections 3.1–3.3 retain its trace. |
| Global finite-entropy solutions for positive diffusion | Section 2.1 adapts the fixed-positive-diffusion construction to periodic spatial form spaces and retains the usual initial-time coupled entropy inequality. |
| One subsequence tending to zero, giving a global weak solution of the identical zero-diffusion system | Sections 3–7 close the density correlation for the actual positive-diffusion family. Section 8 passes the full equations and diagonalizes over integer time intervals. |
| Strong L^2 velocity convergence on finite intervals | Section 2.2 proves finite-mode velocity compactness; Theorem 1.1 records the convergence. |
| Weak L^1 polymer-density convergence | Section 8 proves the stronger conclusion of strong L^1 density convergence. |
| Stress converges to the stress computed from the limiting density | Sections 2.2 and 8 use the uniform Hardy boundary tail and strong density convergence to obtain strong L^1 stress convergence. |
| Spatial transport has no extra defect | Sections 2.2 and 8 pass u_n psi_n by normalization, strong velocity convergence, and truncation. |
| Full configuration drag has no extra defect | Sections 5–7 identify and eliminate the relevant density covariance; Section 8 pairs strongly converging bounded configuration moments with weak L^2 velocity gradients. No corotational replacement is made. |
| Configuration diffusion and zero boundary flux | Sections 6.3 and 8 control configuration collars and pass the square-root diffusion product in the variational identity for tests on the closed ball. |
| Same initial data and usual kinetic-fluid entropy inequality | Section 8 passes the initial terms, gives weak time representatives and a strong initial density trace, and applies lower semicontinuity to the initial-time entropy inequality. |

The manuscript additionally claims strong L^1 density and stress convergence. It does not assume or claim strong convergence of the entire velocity gradient. The nonnegative Stokes defect in Section 5 controls stress-driven gradient oscillation, not the full viscous dissipation defect. An inequality starting at almost every positive time is stated only if that property is inherited from the selected positive-diffusion family; the usual inequality from the prescribed initial time is unconditional.

This is a complete analytic solution claim submitted for independent review. It is not a statement of upstream acceptance or formal verification.

For $`0<a<\pi/2`$, $`\alpha\in\mathbb R`$, and $`m\in\mathbb Z`$, put $`\beta=\tfrac12\tan a`$ and define on $`L^2(-a,a)`$

```math
H_{a,\alpha,m}u=-u''+\frac{8m^2-3-\cos(2x)}{8\cos^2x}\,u,
```



```math
D(H_{a,\alpha,m})=\{u\in H^2(-a,a):u'(\pm a)+(i\alpha\pm\beta)u(\pm a)=0\}.
```

Is $`\sigma(H_{a,\alpha,m})\subset\mathbb R`$ for every such triple? These separated operators represent the Laplace–Beltrami problem on a tubular neighborhood of the equator with the parity-and-time symmetric Robin conditions of the references.

# Target comparison for AIM 424

Original problem: [Reality of the spectrum for a spherical strip with PT-symmetric boundary conditions](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/424-spherical-pt-robin-real-spectrum.md), revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`.

The manuscript's equations (1)--(2) define exactly the original operator and domain. Theorem 1.1 gives an affirmative answer for every triple in the original question.

| Original requirement | Manuscript location | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Every real half-width `0 < a < pi/2` | Introduction; Theorem 1.1 | The interval is fixed arbitrarily throughout; neither excluded endpoint is added. |
| Every real `alpha` | Theorem 1.1; Section 3.3 | The exact boundary determinant is nonzero at every nonreal spectral parameter for every real alpha. |
| Every integer `m` | Propositions 2.3--2.4 | Nonzero integer modes use the positive Fourier comparison; the zero mode uses the first-order factorization. The potential depends on m squared, so both signs are included. |
| Original potential | Introduction before equation (1) | Both the original fraction and its identical secant-squared expression are displayed. |
| Complex Lebesgue `L2(-a,a)` and exact `H2` domain | Introduction, equations (1)--(2) | Both endpoint derivatives are coordinate derivatives, with the original opposite real Robin signs. |
| All spectral indices | Section 2; Lemmas 3.1--3.2 | Strict Robin/Dirichlet interlacing and the canonical products are proved analytically for the full spectra. |
| Entire spectrum contained in the real line | Theorem 1.1; final proof in Section 3.3 | Every nonreal parameter has a unique bounded `L2`-to-`H2` inverse; the realization is dense and closed. |

The argument does not replace the spherical potential by the comparison operator. It retains the exact curvature term and endpoint coefficients. The theorem concerns each separated operator; it makes no parameter-uniform resolvent or singular-endpoint claim.

The problem note's equation (2) and Krejcirik--Siegl's Section 4.4.2 identify the same family. Their zero-potential and sufficiently-large-real-part results are credited in the Introduction. The new manuscript supplies the all-index comparison and the remaining low-spectrum argument; it does not infer priority from a literature search.

The package is a complete solution claim offered for independent mathematical review. Its proof is analytic, with no numerical or formal-verification premise.

records.pr_title: 366: proposed counterexample to literal rapid-decay continuation
records.original_target_statement:
Let $`f\ge0`$ be a smooth solution on $`[0,T)\times\mathbb T^3_x\times\mathbb R^3_v`$, $`T<\infty`$, of the hard-sphere cutoff equation

```math
\partial_tf+v\cdot\nabla_xf=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\int_{\mathbb S^2}|v-v_*|\,[f(v')f(v_*')-f(v)f(v_*)]\,d\sigma\,dv_*,
```

where $`v'=(v+v_*)/2+|v-v_*|\sigma/2`$ and $`v_*'=(v+v_*)/2-|v-v_*|\sigma/2`$; all factors share $`(t,x)`$. Assume $`f(0)`$ and all its derivatives decay faster than any inverse power of $`|v|`$. Suppose constants $`m_0,M_0,E_0>0`$ and $`H_0\in\mathbb R`$ satisfy, for all $`(t,x)`$,

```math
m_0\le\int f\,dv\le M_0,\qquad\int |v|^2f\,dv\le E_0,\qquad\int f\log f\,dv\le H_0.
```

Must $`f`$ extend beyond $`T`$ as a smooth solution with the same rapid velocity decay? No a priori bound on $`f`$ itself or on its derivatives is assumed.

# Target comparison: AIM 366

Original: [Continuation of the cutoff Boltzmann flow from macroscopic bounds](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/366-cutoff-boltzmann-continuation.md), revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`.

Submitted result: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 5.1 of *Loss of rapid velocity decay in a broad smooth class for the cutoff Boltzmann equation*.

| Original requirement | Result and manuscript location | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hard-sphere kernel, full sphere and specified post-collision velocities | Equation (1.1), Section 1; radial normalization in (2.2)–(2.4) | Same model and sphere measure of total area `4 pi` |
| Domain `[0,T) x T^3 x R^3` for finite `T` | Theorem 1.1, Corollary 5.1; restrict a homogeneous radial solution to any `0<T<t_*` | An admissible special case suffices for a counterexample to a universal assertion |
| Nonnegative smooth solution | Sections 4–5; Propositions 4.1–4.2 and compact maximum argument | Joint pointwise smoothness up to time zero and at all finite velocities, including zero |
| Initially rapidly decreasing datum with rapidly decreasing derivatives | Equation (1.3) and Section 5: Gaussian datum | All spatial and velocity derivatives are Schwartz; correction time jets vanish initially |
| Uniform positive lower and finite upper local mass | Equation (1.3), Section 5 | Mass is identically one, so `m_0=M_0=1` |
| Uniform local energy upper bound | Equation (1.4), final part of Section 5 | Finite bound from a uniform `X_6` norm; no energy conservation or energy inequality is asserted |
| Uniform local entropy upper bound | Equation (1.4), final part of Section 5 | Positive and negative entropy parts are finite; upper bound follows from mass and a uniform pointwise bound |
| Extension with rapid velocity decay | Equation (1.5), Corollary 5.1 | Every continuous endpoint extension has a positive `r^-6` tail, which excludes rapid decay |
| Quantifiers and constants | Theorem 1.1, final part of Section 5 | One fixed positive `epsilon` and short interval suffice; all macroscopic bounds are uniform in time and space |
| Imported kinetic existence theorem | None | The construction is proved in the manuscript. The three references are contextual; the exact theorem comparison with Lu–Wennberg remains unverified |

The result is a proposed negative answer to the literal rapid-decay conclusion when “smooth” means joint pointwise smoothness and no energy-admissibility or positive-time Schwartz condition is included in the solution class. The example already continues smoothly in `X_6` across every chosen endpoint `T<t_*`. It therefore does not establish local derivative blowup, failure of critical-weight smooth continuation, or resolution of a conservative/energy-admissible continuation formulation.

Related weak energy-increasing solutions are credited in Section 1. This package makes no novelty or priority claim and does not assert that the literal interpretation settles every conventional conditional-regularity question.

records.pr_title: 141: finite-jet controllability counterexample
records.original_target_statement:
Let $`n\ge3`$ and let $`X_0,\ldots,X_m`$ be real-analytic vector fields near $`0\in\mathbb R^n`$, with $`X_0(0)=0`$. Controls are measurable maps into $`[-1,1]^m`$, and trajectories satisfy

```math
\dot x=X_0(x)+\sum_{j=1}^m u_j(t)X_j(x).
```

Call the system small-time locally controllable at $`0`$ if, for every sufficiently small $`t>0`$, its points reachable from $`0`$ in time at most $`t`$ contain a neighborhood of $`0`$.

If this property holds, must there exist an integer $`N`$ such that every real-analytic tuple $`Y_0,\ldots,Y_m`$ with

```math
D^\alpha Y_j(0)=D^\alpha X_j(0)\quad
(0\le j\le m,\ |\alpha|\le N)
```

has the same controllability property with the same control set? Here $`\alpha`$ is a multi-index; $`N`$ may depend on the original system.

# Comparison with the original target

Target: [AIM 141 at a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/141-finite-jet-small-time-control.md).
The paper gives a negative answer by an analytic counterexample.

| Original requirement | Paper result and location | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| All real-analytic systems in dimensions n>=3 | Theorem 1 uses one polynomial system in R^5 | One admissible counterexample negates the universal implication; no n=3/4 classification |
| Equilibrium drift at zero | Displayed original and perturbed drifts vanish at zero | Same hypothesis |
| Measurable controls in the fixed cube | Theorem 1 and proof use (u,v) in [-1,1]^2 throughout | Same control class and bounds |
| Original small-time local controllability | Theorem 1 invokes the exact full-neighborhood result in Jin's earlier Theorem 1; Section 2 identifies its signed-loop and four-coordinate steering proof | Full Euclidean neighborhood, not an axis-only premise |
| One original tuple before choosing N | The system in equation (1) remains fixed | Original tuple independent of N |
| Every prescribed finite Taylor order N | Choose k>=1 with 2k>N | All finite N, not a finite computational range |
| Every field and multi-index derivative through total order N | Controlled fields are unchanged; the drift difference is x_5^(2k)e_4 | Complete matching N-jet |
| The matched tuple should retain controllability | Equations (5)--(9) prove that every fourth-axis endpoint in all sufficiently small durations has nonnegative fourth coordinate | The perturbed tuple is not small-time locally controllable |
| Reachability in time at most t | The proof explicitly takes the union over every duration 0<=T<=t<=tau_k | Same at-most-time definition |
| External theorem applicability | Section 2 states Jin's Lemma 2 with C^2/Lipschitz/third-derivative bounds and all six zero endpoint jets before applying it | Exact credited mathematical inputs |

The original system and its logarithmic estimate are prior results. The added
argument establishes an obstruction for each high-order positive drift
perturbation uniformly over every admissible control, then matches the full
finite jet. The package does not claim human peer review, formal verification
or a result for each individual dimension n>=3.

records.pr_title: 429: proposed sharp transmission Weyl remainder
records.original_target_statement:
Let $`\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d`$, $`d\ge2`$, be bounded, connected, with $`C^\infty`$ boundary, and fix a constant $`n>1`$. A nonzero number $`z`$ is an interior transmission eigenvalue if nonzero $`(u,v)`$ solve

```math
\Delta u+nzu=0,\quad\Delta v+zv=0\quad\text{in }\Omega,
```



```math
u=v,\qquad\partial_\nu u=\partial_\nu v\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega.
```

Use algebraic multiplicity for the closed transmission operator $`A(u,v)=(-n^{-1}\Delta u,-\Delta v)`$ on $`L^2(\Omega)\oplus L^2(\Omega)`$, with domain consisting of pairs whose distributional Laplacians lie in $`L^2`$ and whose Dirichlet and normal traces agree in the generalized trace sense. Algebraic multiplicity is the dimension of the Riesz spectral projection of $`A`$ around the nonzero eigenvalue. Let $`N(r)`$ count its nonzero eigenvalues with $`|z|\le r^2`$, including multiplicities. Must

```math
N(r)=\frac{\omega_d}{(2\pi)^d}|\Omega|(1+n^{d/2})r^d+O_{\Omega,n}(r^{d-1})\qquad(r\to\infty),
```

where $`\omega_d=|B_1|`$? This is the constant-index isotropic case of Vodev’s conjecture; no convexity is imposed.

# Comparison with problem 042

This comparison uses the accompanying finished manuscript and the
[original public problem at its fixed revision](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/042-accurate-bidiagonal-svd.md).
The contribution is an analytic floating-arithmetic construction, accompanied
by research software and ordinary finite numerical validation.

| Original requirement | Finished manuscript | Scope and interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real upper bidiagonal input, including signed entries | Section 2; Theorem 2.1 | The stored binary64 input is the mathematical input. Reducible, singular and repeated-value cases are included. |
| Any k distinct requested ordered ranks | Section 2 and Algorithm 1 | 1 <= k <= n; output order follows the caller's requested ranks. Repeated values allow the stated orthonormal-basis freedom. |
| Unit left and right vectors | Equation (1), Theorem 2.1 | A nonzero floating carrier x represents the exact direction x/sqrt(x^T x). This convention is explicit; the raw array is not claimed to have exactly unit norm. |
| Nonnegative estimates and ordered-value accuracy | Theorem 2.1, equation (2); Section 6 | The common error constant is 128 for represented unit directions. |
| Both singular-vector equations | Theorem 2.1, equation (3); Section 6 | Both residuals are at most 128 n epsilon \|\|B\|\|_2, including the zero-value branch. |
| Separate left and right orthogonality, independent of gaps/clusters | Theorem 2.1, equation (4); Sections 4 and 6 | Pairwise inner products are at most 128 n epsilon. The common near-zero cut handles the mixed left-direction products. |
| O(nk) arithmetic work | Algorithm 1 cost discussion; Theorem 2.1; Sections 3-6 | Fixed-format interpretation: O(p^4 nk) operations on O(p)-bit numbers, conservatively O(p^6 nk) bit work. This is O(nk) in n,k after fixing p; no precision-uniform O(nk) claim is made. |
| Small epsilon n; exclude overflow/underflow | Section 2 | epsilon=2^-p, integer 16 <= p <= 53, n epsilon <= 1/64. Correct rounding, protected exact indices and power-of-two scaling are specified. Binary64 input/output storage is fixed. |
| Actual floating arrays | Corollary 6.1 | Raw arrays satisfy value/residual/orthogonality bounds with conservative constant 256 and squared-norm defect at most 8 epsilon. This is distinct from exact unit-direction semantics. |
| Public mathematical dependencies | References [4]-[5] at their printed theorem locators | The finite-dimensional spectral theorem and Cauchy derivative estimate are used under the stated finite-dimensional/analytic hypotheses. The construction and rounding bounds are in the manuscript. |

The sufficient core precision is 67584+2880p bits, or 220224 bits at p=53.
The paper claims a fixed-format complexity construction, not practical speed
superiority. The Python/C++ implementation has finite allocation, index and
resource limits, documented separately. Its optional exact rational checker
validates an individual original input/output pair at additional cost; tests
and the two fixed matrices do not prove the universal theorem.

The claim is submitted for independent mathematical review under the explicit
arithmetic and represented-direction conventions above. No extension to
complex matrices, formal verification, independent human certification, or
repository acceptance is asserted.

records.pr_title: 193: proposed solution of the Gaussian polymer moment spectrum
records.original_target_statement:
Let $`(S_n)`$ be simple random walk on $`\mathbb Z^3`$ from zero and let $`\omega_{n,x}`$ be iid standard Gaussians independent of the walk. For $`\beta>0`$, set

```math
W_N^\beta=E_S\exp\!\left(\sum_{n=1}^N(\beta\omega_{n,S_n}-\beta^2/2)\right),\qquad
p^*(\beta)=\sup\{p\ge1:\sup_N\mathbb E_\omega[(W_N^\beta)^p]<\infty\}.
```

Write $`W_\infty^\beta`$ for the nonnegative martingale limit and define $`\beta_c=\sup\{\beta:P(W_\infty^\beta>0)=1\}`$. Is $`\beta\mapsto p^*(\beta)`$ a continuous strictly decreasing bijection from $`(0,\beta_c]`$ onto $`[5/3,\infty)`$? Continuity at $`\beta_c`$ means continuity from the left.

records.pr_title: 185: proposed resolution — CO phase selection for a stirred catalytic surface model
records.original_target_statement:
Consider states $`0`$ (vacant), $`1`$ (CO) and $`2`$ (oxygen) on $`\mathbb Z^2`$. A vacant site becomes $`1`$ at rate $`p`$. Each unordered nearest-neighbor pair in state $`(0,0)`$ changes to $`(2,2)`$ at rate $`q/4`$, and each pair containing one $`1`$ and one $`2`$ changes to $`(0,0)`$ at rate $`r/4`$. Each pair also exchanges its states at rate $`\gamma`$. Assume $`p>q>0`$, $`0<r<\infty`$ and $`0<\gamma<\infty`$.

Let the initial site states be independent and identically distributed with $`P(\eta_0(0)=1)>0`$. For every such initial law and every choice of the parameters above, is it true that, for every finite $`K\subset\mathbb Z^2`$,

```math
\lim_{t\to\infty}P(\eta_t(x)=1\text{ for all }x\in K)=1?
```

# Correspondence with AIM Problem 185

Original target:
[Selection of the carbon-monoxide poisoning phase](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/185-catalytic-carbon-monoxide-poisoning.md),
revision a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22.

The submitted manuscript is *CO phase selection for a stirred catalytic
surface model*, by Kaiwen Jin. Its Theorem 1 claims the entire target.

| Original requirement | Location in the manuscript | Correspondence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| States vacant, CO and oxygen on the infinite lattice Z2 | Section 1 model; Appendix A construction | Same process and domain |
| A vacant site becomes CO at rate p | Section 1 transition table; equation (4) | Same site rate |
| Each unordered vacant neighbor pair becomes two oxygen atoms at rate q/4 | Section 1 table and O(t) in Section 2 | Same pair convention and rate |
| An unordered mixed CO/oxygen pair becomes vacant at rate r/4 | Section 1 table; equation (3) and R(t) | Same pair convention and rate |
| Each pair exchanges states at finite positive rate gamma | Section 1 table; Lemma 2 and equation (9) | All effective exchanges are included |
| Every p>q>0 and every finite positive r,gamma | Section 1 hypotheses, equations (7)--(9), Theorem 1 | No additional parameter threshold or limiting regime |
| Every iid initial law with positive CO density | Theorem 1 and its proof in Section 3 | No lower positive-density bound |
| Every finite K, with all-CO probability tending to one as real time tends to infinity | Theorem 1, equation (1), final proof paragraph | Same quantifiers and conclusion |

Theorem 1 also proves that every site eventually remains CO almost surely.
The sitewise random times need not have a finite maximum over the infinite
lattice. This additional conclusion is not a claim of simultaneous global
absorption at a finite time.

Durrett and Swindle's *Coexistence results for catalysts* (1994),
Theorem 1 and its proof on pp. 490--492, supply the model and the
signed-density/vacancy estimate credited in Section 2. The manuscript supplies
the reaction count, finite-change and marked-field phase-selection argument.
The pinned Durrett book's Open Problem 5.4.6 is cited for the question;
the result here is stated for the iid initial-law class specified by this
AIM target, without asserting its broader initial-data formulation.

This is a full solution claim offered for mathematical review. It is not an
announcement of upstream acceptance or a formal proof certificate.

records.pr_title: 328: proposed counterexample for Fitch reconstruction under a molecular clock
records.original_target_statement:
Let $`r\ge5`$ be an integer and let $`T`$ be a finite rooted tree with at least two leaves, in which every internal vertex has exactly two children. Write $`\rho`$ for its root and $`X`$ for its leaf set. Assign each edge $`e`$ a finite length $`\ell_e\ge0`$, and require every path from $`\rho`$ to a leaf to have the same total length $`H`$. This is the molecular-clock, or ultrametric, assumption.

Generate states $`\sigma_v\in\{1,\ldots,r\}`$ on the vertices as follows. Choose $`\sigma_\rho`$ uniformly. Along an edge of length $`\ell`$, evolve a continuous-time Markov chain for time $`\ell`$ with generator

```math
Q_{ij}=\begin{cases}
-1,&i=j,\\
1/(r-1),&i\ne j.
\end{cases}
```

Branches evolve independently conditional on their parent states. This is the symmetric Neyman $`r`$-state model, with expected substitution rate one. In particular, the probability that any specified leaf has the root's state is

```math
q_r(H)=\frac1r+\frac{r-1}{r}\exp\!\left(-\frac{rH}{r-1}\right).
```

Observe the states at all leaves of the known tree. The Fitch parsimony estimator constructs a set $`S_v`$ at each vertex: $`S_x=\{\sigma_x\}`$ at a leaf, and, for children $`u,w`$ of an internal vertex $`v`$,

```math
S_v=\begin{cases}
S_u\cap S_w,&S_u\cap S_w\ne\varnothing,\\
S_u\cup S_w,&S_u\cap S_w=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
```

Choose $`\widehat\sigma_\rho`$ uniformly from $`S_\rho`$. Its accuracy includes both the random character generated on the tree and this final tie-breaking choice.

**Does every such tree and length assignment satisfy**

```math
\Pr\{\widehat\sigma_\rho=\sigma_\rho\}\ \ge\ q_r(H)?
```

Thus, does using all the leaves with Fitch parsimony perform at least as well as guessing the root state from any one leaf? This is the unresolved $`r>4`$ portion of the Li–Steel–Zhang conjecture. The same inequality is proved for $`r=2,3,4`$. The estimator uses the topology and leaf states; the edge lengths specify the probability model but are not inputs to its recursion. The question concerns one character on each finite tree, rather than an asymptotic sequence-length or tree-estimation guarantee.
records.target_reference_section:
1. Guoliang Li, Mike Steel and Louxin Zhang, *More Taxa Are Not Necessarily Better for the Reconstruction of Ancestral Character States*, Systematic Biology 57(4) (2008), 647–653, [published paper](https://doi.org/10.1080/10635150802203898); [accessible published PDF](https://www2.gwu.edu/~clade/bisc%20207/LiEtAl2008.pdf). # Comparison with AIM Problem 328

Frozen statement: [328, revision a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/328-fitch-ultrametric-ancestral-accuracy.md).

The original assertion is universal over every integer r>=5 and every finite
rooted strictly binary tree with at least two leaves, finite nonnegative edge
lengths and equal root-to-leaf height H. Under the specified rate-one symmetric
Neyman model, uniform root and uniform final Fitch tie breaking, it asks whether
accuracy is at least q_r(H)=1/r+(r-1)exp(-rH/(r-1))/r.

Theorem 1 supplies an admissible r=20 counterexample, hence negates that universal
assertion. No positive theorem or failure classification for other alphabets
is claimed.

| Original clause | Manuscript location and exact fulfillment |
|---|---|
| Integer r>=5 | Theorem 1 chooses r=20. |
| Finite tree; at least two leaves; two children at each internal vertex | Theorem 1 specifies rho with children a,v and v with children b,c. |
| Finite nonnegative lengths | Equation (3) specifies four strictly positive logarithmic lengths. |
| Equal root-to-leaf heights | Theorem 1 and start of proof give log16+log(5/4)=log20 and H=(19/20)log20. |
| Exact generator and rate | Equation (1) has diagonal -1 and off-diagonal 1/19 at r=20; equation (5) preserves that normalization. |
| Uniform root and conditional branch independence | Section 1 states the model; Section 2 conditions on root state 1, uses parent-conditioned terminal independence and branch independence, then removes root conditioning by label symmetry. |
| Literal Fitch recursion and uniform final tie | Section 1 defines the sets and final choice; equations (7)-(9) use the full cherry set and exact singleton/union cases. |
| One character on a known tree | The entire calculation uses the three observed states on one specified finite tree, with no sequence or topology-estimation limit. |
| Compare against any one leaf | Equations (2)-(4), equal heights and equation (5) give q_20(H)=39/400 for every leaf. |
| Strict failure | Equations (4) and (9) give 38829/400000 <39000/400000, deficit 171/400000. |

The proposed resolution is analytic and self-contained. The supplementary exact
verifier checks the finite arithmetic; it is not a substitute for the written
proof. Submission of this package does not establish upstream acceptance,

records.original_target_statement:
Let $`\tau=\{0=\tau_0<\tau_1<\cdots\}`$ be a renewal process with iid gaps satisfying

```math
P(\tau_1=n)=\frac{n^{-5/4}}{\sum_{m\ge1}m^{-5/4}}\quad(n\ge1).
```

Let $`(\omega_n)`$ be independent standard Gaussians, independent of $`\tau`$. Define

```math
Z_{N,h}^{\beta,\omega}=E_\tau\exp\!\left(\sum_{n=1}^N(\beta\omega_n+h)\mathbf1_{\{n\in\tau\}}\right),\qquad
F(\beta,h)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\mathbb E_\omega\log Z_{N,h}^{\beta,\omega}.
```

Put $`h_c(\beta)=\inf\{h:F(\beta,h)>0\}`$. The normalized partition function $`W_N=Z_{N,-\beta^2/2}^{\beta,\omega}`$ is a nonnegative martingale; write $`W_\infty`$ for its almost-sure limit.

For every $`\beta>0`$, does $`P(W_\infty=0)=1`$ imply $`h_c(\beta)>-\beta^2/2`$?

records.original_target_statement:
Let $`(M,g)`$ be a connected, complete, noncompact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary. For $`j\in\{0,+\}`$, let $`V_j\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)`$ be bounded below and let $`H_j=-\Delta_g+V_j`$ denote its Friedrichs realization on $`L^2(M,d\mathrm{vol}_g)`$. Assume $`H_j\ge0`$ and $`\inf\sigma(H_j)=0`$. Write $`k_j(t,x,y)>0`$ for the heat kernel of $`e^{-tH_j}`$.
Assume, for some distinct $`x_*,y_*\in M`$,

```math
\int_0^\infty k_+(t,x_*,y_*)\,dt<\infty,
\qquad
\int_0^\infty k_0(t,x_*,y_*)\,dt=\infty,
```

and assume $`\ker_{L^2}H_0=\{0\}`$. These assumptions specify a subcritical operator and a null-critical reference operator. Must

```math
\lim_{t\to\infty}\ \sup_{(x,y)\in K}
\frac{k_+(t,x,y)}{k_0(t,x,y)}=0
\quad\text{for every compact }K\subset M\times M?
```

No pointwise ordering between $`V_+`$ and $`V_0`$ is assumed.

# Comparison with AIM Problem 217

Target: [the complete problem statement at revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/217-critical-subcritical-heat-ratio.md).

Proposed resolution: the [manuscript](paper/main.pdf), Theorem 1.1, gives a counterexample to the full universal question. Section 1 restates the original hypotheses and explains why a diagonal test of the conclusion is admissible even though the integral-test points must be distinct.

| Original requirement | Constructed object or verification | Manuscript location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connected, complete, noncompact smooth manifold without boundary | The Euclidean line with its usual metric | Theorem 1.1 and the following paragraph, pp. 1–2 |
| Two smooth real potentials bounded below | One fixed nonnegative compact bump `q`; one fixed `V_0 = w'' + (w')²`. Both are smooth and bounded | Lemma 2.3, p. 3; Section 3, pp. 4–5 |
| Friedrichs realizations on the same square-integrable space | Both operators act on `L²(R,dx)`, with the standard bounded-potential form/domain | Theorem 1.1, p. 1; start of Section 2, p. 2 |
| Both operators nonnegative | Positivity of `q`; factorization of the reference quadratic form | Lemma 2.3, p. 3; equation (16), p. 4 |
| Both spectral bottoms zero | Translated free test functions for the numerator; explicit resistance-tent tests for the final reference | Lemma 2.3, p. 3; Section 3, p. 6 |
| One fixed pair of distinct points with finite numerator integral | The pair `(0,1)`; explicit positive zero-energy solution and finite Green limit | Lemmas 2.2–2.3, p. 3; Appendix A, pp. 6–8 |
| The same pair with infinite reference integral | Preserved unit zero intervals make both resistance integrals infinite; the exact Green exhaustion gives divergence at `(0,1)` | Equations (20)–(21), p. 5; Section 3, p. 6; Appendix A |
| Reference has no nonzero square-integrable zero mode | A form-zero vector must be a multiple of `exp(w)`; this function is at least one everywhere | Factorization discussion, p. 4, applied to the final reference on p. 5 |
| No potential ordering is assumed | No ordering is imposed; the constructed potential difference takes both signs | End of Section 3, p. 6 |
| Claimed limit for every compact subset of the product manifold | At times tending to infinity, the quotient at `(0,0)` is at least the sequence index; choose the compact singleton `{(0,0)}` | Theorem 1.1, equations (3)–(4), pp. 1–2; concluding estimate, p. 6 |

The construction yields one fixed pair, rather than a sequence of counterexamples depending on the observation time. Each finite approximation has its own strictly positive gap. Its time is selected first, followed by a radius that protects the estimate under all later exterior changes. Only local stabilization is used to define the final smooth potential. The final reference has spectral bottom zero.

The conclusion is an infinite limsup along a sequence, which already negates the proposed zero limit. The manuscript makes no claim about all-time quotient asymptotics or about the ordered nonnegative-perturbation comparison. Its citations distinguish the original question from the conditional results. This is a complete analytic counterexample claim submitted for independent review; no numerical or formal evidence is substituted for its proof.

records.original_target_statement:
Let $`0<\alpha<1`$ and let $`K:(0,\infty)^2\to[0,\infty)`$ be continuous and symmetric. Assume that for some $`0<c<C<\infty`$ and continuous $`\ell>0`$,

```math
c(x^\alpha y+xy^\alpha)\le K(x,y)\le C(x^\alpha y+xy^\alpha),\quad\lim_{y\to\infty}K(x,y)/y=\ell(x),\quad cx^\alpha\le\ell(x)\le Cx^\alpha.
```

Let $`\mu_0`$ be a finite nonnegative measure on $`(0,\infty)`$ with $`\int x\,d\mu_0=1`$. A Flory solution is a family of finite nonnegative measures with nonincreasing particle number and mass $`M_1(t)=\int x\,d\mu_t`$, satisfying for every $`\phi\in C_c([0,\infty))`$

```math
\langle\mu_t,\phi\rangle=\langle\mu_0,\phi\rangle+\frac12\int_0^t\!\iint K(x,y)[\phi(x+y)-\phi(x)-\phi(y)]\,d\mu_s(x)\,d\mu_s(y)\,ds-\int_0^t(1-M_1(s))\langle\mu_s,\ell\phi\rangle\,ds.
```

For every such solution whose gelation time $`T_g=\inf\{t:M_1(t)<1\}`$ satisfies $`0<T_g<\infty`$, must $`M_1`$ be continuous at $`T_g`$, with $`M_1(T_g)=\lim_{t\downarrow T_g}M_1(t)=1`$?

records.original_target_statement:
Let $`\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d`$, $`d\ge2`$, be connected, unbounded, and uniformly $`C^{2,\gamma}`$ for some $`0<\gamma<1`$: its boundary has graph charts of a common positive radius with uniformly bounded $`C^{2,\gamma}`$ norms. Let $`f\in C^{1,\gamma}([0,\infty))`$ satisfy $`f(0)=f(1)=0`$, $`f'(0)>0`$, $`f>0`$ on $`(0,1)`$, $`f<0`$ on $`(1,\infty)`$, and $`f(s)/s`$ strictly decreasing on $`(0,1]`$. For each fixed $`\beta\in[0,1)`$, is there at most one bounded positive classical solution of

```math
-\Delta u=f(u)\quad\hbox{in }\Omega,\qquad \beta\partial_nu+(1-\beta)u=0\quad\hbox{on }\partial\Omega?
```

Here $`n`$ is the outward normal, and $`\beta=0`$ denotes Dirichlet boundary conditions. No periodicity or spectral-gap assumption at spatial infinity is made.

# Target comparison: AIM 379

Target: [Uniqueness of strong-KPP equilibria on general unbounded domains](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/379-strong-kpp-unbounded-uniqueness.md), repository revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`.

Result: Theorem 1 of [the manuscript](paper/main.pdf) is an analytic counterexample to the universal assertion. The following map is based on that finished manuscript and the public target.

| Original requirement | Manuscript location and supplied object | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dimension d >= 2 | Theorem 1 and Section 3 use d=21, with x in R^20 and y in R | One allowed dimension suffices for a counterexample |
| Connected, unbounded domain | Section 4, equation (11); a strip between two graphs, connected through y=0 | Exact domain class |
| Common-radius uniformly bounded C^{2,gamma} boundary charts | Section 4: global graphs, bounded derivatives through order 3 and graph separation at least pi | gamma=1/2, common chart radius and uniform norms |
| Homogeneous f in C^{1,gamma}([0,infinity)) | Section 1, equation (2); bounded reaction with bounded Lipschitz derivative | gamma=1/2, including the global bounded-norm convention |
| f(0)=f(1)=0, f'(0)>0, positive on (0,1), negative above 1 | Equation (2) and the following verification | Every sign clause holds |
| f(s)/s strictly decreasing on (0,1] | Equation (2): ratio 1-s on this interval | Exact required interval |
| Fixed beta in [0,1) | Section 1 after Theorem 1 takes beta=0, zero Dirichlet trace | An admitted parameter; no other Robin claim |
| Bounded positive classical solutions | Theorem 1; Lemma 2; Section 4 constructs U and T, locally C^{2,1/2} up to the true boundary and between 0 and 1 | Exact solution concept |
| At most one such solution | Equations (12) and (14) and the last comparison in Section 4: U(x,0)>=q^{-1}>Bq^{-2}>=T(x,0) for sufficiently large fixed q | Uniqueness fails on the same domain with the same reaction and boundary parameter |
| No periodicity or spectral-gap condition | Lemma 2 uses bounded exhaustions and fixed-patch estimates; Sections 3-4 give explicit barriers | No such extra hypothesis is imposed |
| Uniform constants and behavior at infinity | Section 3 fixes R=10^6 and b=20000; Section 4 fixes finite B from one compact collar before choosing separation points | One domain and fixed constants, not a changing-domain limit |
| Imported elliptic theory | Lemma 2 cites Gilbarg-Trudinger Theorem 8.9, Corollary 8.36, Theorem 9.19 (k=1), Lemma 6.18, Corollaries 6.3/6.7; Section 2 cites its weak chain rule | Identity principal coefficients, bounded forces, zero true-boundary data and fixed local patches meet the stated conditions |

The quantifier conclusion is a negation: existence of one admissible (d, domain, f, beta) with two distinct equilibria disproves uniqueness asserted for every admissible choice. It does not classify all remaining choices.

The introduction credits Berestycki-Graham's original conjecture and conditional uniqueness theorem, their later open-question formulation, and Rossi-Tough's dimension results and shrinking-obstacle counterexamples. The paper's added construction is the uniformly smooth graph domain and its explicit barrier argument. Independent mathematical review is pending.

records.original_target_statement:
Fix $`n\ge2`$, $`0<s<1`$, and $`0<\lambda\le\Lambda`$. Let $`\{K_a\}_{a\in A}`$ be any family of even measurable kernels satisfying

```math
\lambda|y|^{-n-2s}\le K_a(y)\le\Lambda|y|^{-n-2s}.
```

Set $`L_au(x)=\mathop{\mathrm{PV}}\nolimits\int[u(x)-u(x+y)]K_a(y)dy`$ and $`Iu=\inf_{a\in A}(-L_au)`$.

Is there a finite $`p_*=p_*(n,s,\lambda,\Lambda)`$ such that, for every $`p>\max\{2,p_*\}`$, bounded viscosity solutions of $`Iu=f`$ in $`B_1`$ with smooth $`f`$ satisfy

```math
\|u\|_{W^{2s,p}(B_{1/2})}\le C\bigl(\|u\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}+\|f\|_{L^p(B_1)}\bigr),
```

where $`C`$ depends only on $`n,s,p,\lambda,\Lambda`$? Use the Slobodeckij Sobolev space for noninteger $`2s`$ and the ordinary Sobolev space when $`2s=1`$. The estimate must be uniform over the kernels and must not depend on stronger norms of $`f`$.

# Comparison with Problem 463

Target: [Calderón–Zygmund estimates for general concave nonlocal equations](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/blob/a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22/problems/463-concave-nonlocal-calderon-zygmund.md), revision `a153f469ee0ea64e876b2ad97c79d252c19a3e22`.

The submitted result is an analytic counterexample to the proposed estimate over the general kernel class. The manuscript uses `sigma = 2s`. For every strict ellipticity pair `0 < lambda < Lambda` and every finite `p > max(2,n/sigma)`, Theorem 1.1 contradicts any proposed constant depending only on the stated parameters. Consequently no finite large-p threshold yields the asserted estimate for this general class. The equal-constant isotropic class is outside the negative assertion.

| Original requirement | Manuscript location | Comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `n >= 2`, `0 < s < 1` | Introduction and Theorem 1.1; `sigma = 2s` | Every original dimension and order; the proof uses `n > sigma`, automatic here. |
| Any even measurable translation invariant kernels between the two power-law bounds | Equations (1.1), (2.2), (2.3), Section 2 | Exact pointwise bounds with the same fixed constants. Kernels depend only on the jump variable and can be smooth away from zero. Compact finite dimensional disk controls are allowed index sets. |
| Sign convention `I = inf_a(-L_a)` with positive `L_a` | Equation (1.2), Section 2 | Exact agreement, including the symmetric-integral factor. |
| Bounded viscosity solutions in the unit ball, smooth right side | Proposition 4.1 and following paragraph | The examples are globally smooth bounded classical solutions with smooth bounded right side. Positivity of kernels gives the viscosity touching inequalities. |
| Interior `W^(2s,p)` norm: Slobodeckij for noninteger order and ordinary Sobolev at order one | Introduction; Proposition 4.1; final proof in Section 5 | All three order regimes are handled in precisely those spaces. |
| Constant uniform over kernel families and depending on the right side only through its `Lp` norm | Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 4.1 | Kernel families vary along the construction while ellipticity constants stay fixed. The forcing tends to zero in `Lp`; its stronger norms are not bounded uniformly. |
| A finite threshold valid for every sufficiently large finite p | Theorem 1.1, Section 5 | Failure for every finite `p > max(2,n/(2s))` rules out each proposed finite threshold at strict ellipticity. No endpoint claim is made. |
| Full global supremum term on the right | Proposition 4.1 and concentrated potentials in Section 5 | Convergence and boundedness hold on the whole space, not just the interior domain. |

The proof is analytic. No numerical experiment, formal proof certificate, human review or upstream acceptance is claimed. The references in the introduction provide context and restricted comparisons; the construction and the Riesz-potential identity are proved in the manuscript.
